C-QUICKLOOK-CONTENT-BOUNDARY.Summary: Make the separately installed QuickLook preview render untrusted Markdown without executing document-controlled active content or accessing remote resources.
C-QUICKLOOK-CONTENT-BOUNDARY.Problem: The preview currently enables markdown-it HTML, inserts its output into innerHTML, embeds the Markdown string inside an executable script, and uses an unrestricted WKWebView with network-client entitlement. A document can therefore cross from data into active preview content. No native exploit or arbitrary native-file access is claimed by this specification.

Goals.R-1: Keep all document-controlled Markdown and titles in a data boundary. Neither HTML event handlers, active elements, nor closing-script sequences may execute document-controlled JavaScript.
Goals.R-2: Permit only the packaged rendering scripts and styles. Block remote subresources, frames, forms, popups and document-driven navigation; the preview must not silently open an external application.
Goals.R-3: Preserve headings, paragraphs, tables, fenced-code highlighting, Unicode, links as readable content and packaged resources. Define the local-image policy explicitly and prove allowed local previews do not broaden access beyond the selected document's authorized resource scope.
Goals.R-4: Prove the repaired boundary in an isolated native WKWebView fixture, with independent execution and network observations, and retain the original failure evidence.

Constraints.Constraint: Work only on the separate MarkQuickLook component and narrowly owned verification. Do not change the main Mark renderer, IPC, document-save behavior, dependency versions or production signing identity.

The proposed initial policy disables raw HTML in markdown-it. This is an intentional compatibility change: raw HTML becomes readable escaped text. Do not introduce an HTML sanitizer dependency or a partial regex sanitizer.
Use a restrictive CSP and a native navigation policy in addition to safe data embedding. A script nonce does not make interpolated untrusted content safe.
Remove the preview's network-client entitlement if native verification confirms all intended local rendering remains functional. Never compensate by broadening filesystem or network capabilities.
Native tests must use a separate fixture and output directory. Do not register or replace the installed owner extension or change the owner's default preview association.
No version change, production signing, release tag, dispatch or publication is authorized.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Supporting arbitrary raw HTML, remote images, embedded websites, active SVG, remote fonts or external navigation from QuickLook.
A light/dark redesign, packaging overhaul, main-app security audit, or repair of the local QA-builder finding.
Claiming owner acceptance or production extension installation from an automated WKWebView fixture.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A failing-first fixture demonstrates document-controlled execution on the unchanged renderer using harmless in-memory markers. The repaired renderer leaves markers absent for event handlers, script terminators, mixed-case terminators, active SVG, iframe/srcdoc, object/embed, forms and dangerous URL schemes.
Hostile title, quotes, backslashes, Unicode line separators and Markdown containing closing-script sequences remain literal data and do not break packaged rendering.

Native navigation policy refuses external main-frame/subframe navigation and new-window requests. A controlled loopback observer receives no remote-image, fetch, beacon, frame, form or navigation request.

Positive fixtures show correct headings, a table, fenced-code highlighting and Unicode without remote requests. Allowed local-resource cases and blocked outside-scope cases have explicit expected results.

The extension builds without production signing in an isolated target. The compiled native fixture records revision, source digest, binary identity, result for each case and network/execution observations. Existing installed apps and extensions remain unchanged.

The affected runtime files have synchronized file-local contracts and routed GRACE ownership/verification; selected target/final gates pass without changed assertions, longer deadlines or hidden failures.

AffectedAreas.Area: New narrowly scoped QuickLook verification fixtures under tests/quicklook and their runner under tools; exact paths and module ownership belong to the completed plan.
.grace/graph/index.xml, its affected routed document, .grace/verification/index.xml and its affected routed document, only for QuickLook ownership.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Failing-first harmless content-execution receipt; repaired native WKWebView positive/negative matrix; independent loopback request count; isolated unsigned build identity; exact owner acceptance still pending.
The completed plan must name the exact runner command and measure its gate budget before approval. Browser emulation and source-string scans do not establish the native content boundary.

Assumptions.Assumption: Raw HTML compatibility is intentionally traded for a smaller auditable boundary. This proposal remains draft until owner approval.
The standalone extension is not currently represented as a routed module. Its plan must allocate unused ownership anchors rather than attach unrelated runtime files to an existing module.
